sections.value:
**Performance: pass-with-notes** at `2d2f04e592bc405fa958f8954fa86f0a94748cad`.

Full compaction-wake cost review, including round-2 tracking, holdings-error and in-flight supersession repairs. No new loop, timer or direct executable site: the work rides the existing nominal 60-second PA watchdog round.

**Per round:** one pending-compactions query matching the partial index, plus its schema check. It is empty when no decisions remain, not a per-seat fleet query. The round holds the pending vector and searches the already-read seat vector per row: O(P*N) comparisons in the worst case, with no new registry read.

Newest rows within each seat drive delivery/event reads. Live delivered rows pay up to two query calls: delivery outcome by msg_id, then started_since; an undelivered row only the former, and gone/superseded/blocked older rows can skip them. Supersession reuses the newer row's delivery result in memory and adds **no query**. A settled-age idle candidate adds one two-kind queue peek and open-role/open-claim reads, including sorting/formatting held labels.

**"Indexed" is not constant work:** delivery lookup narrows by seat/kind but filters JSON msg_id while scanning retained outcomes, not a dedicated msg-id index. started_since is bounded by delivery sequence/four kinds. Queue peek can materialize a queued payload; holdings/claims and wake/audit bytes scale with returned data. Schema checks are additional to those quoted query counts.

**Per compact request:** an owned schema-checked INSERT OR IGNORE transaction commits before control admission; failure refuses the compact. Replays can still pay a no-change transaction. Unlike round 1, insert no longer supersedes older pending rows. One successful conditional settlement UPDATE happens later; failed attempts can retry per round. A row left without admission is normally retired as undelivered once it is examined after one hour.

Multiple pending rows may now coexist for a seat. The one-hour check is not a universal age/memory bound: older rows wait behind newer in-flight rows, and read failures remain pending. No pending-row cap/pruning was added. Settled history retains one row per unique tracked compaction, O(total compactions), outside the pending index.

**Wake:** settlement is persisted before sending. This bounds each compaction to at most one wake attempt, not guaranteed delivery: refused/failed/cancelled-after-settlement sends do not retry. Existing delivery does one normal resume message, one parent FYI when applicable, and an audit; its existing persistence/liveness/process work is not made process-free. The five-minute settle interval is not a measured completion or end-to-end latency guarantee.

The new try_holdings_of propagates assignment-read failure to Wait rather than permanently deciding holds-nothing. Before-admission owned tracking prevents an admitted compact lacking its row. These repairs add no periodic task; successful admission/settlement writes are per event, not steady-state writes.

**CI:** exact-head [42420467930](https://github.com/AI-Substrate/pij-fleet/actions/runs/42420467930) succeeds. JUnit confirms **nine daemon compaction cases**, the core message case and all six spawn guards; **2,180 executed cases, zero failures/errors**. Verified failed tracking admission, dropped callers, failed holdings recovery, in-flight/new-compaction behavior, queue/no-holder conditions and restart dedup. Tests use simulated event times, not live compaction timing. Latest Delivers **42420469571** succeeds.

Migration 0044 is above main's 43. No local build, test, mutation, runtime probe or worktree edit. **After-deploy readings remain owed:** same-incarnation 60-second launch/CPU/RSS window and 20-second machine sample; legitimate wake latency/failure/retention evidence is still unmeasured.

**F112 is separate, not this PR's blocker:** the supplied before +119 launches/60s contains +100 legacy tap-writer ps. Its source/cost violation is recorded in governance note `4029f72`; compare rates and per-site deltas without subtracting counters across a daemon bounce.
